claims.claim_ar: الواو في «وَتِلْكَ» واو استئنافية تدخل لاستئناف الكلام وبثِّ التوكيد والانتقال إلى بيان الحجة.
claims.claim_en: The initial waw in «وَتِلْكَ» functions as a waw of resumption (waaw istinaaf), pausing the previous discourse and emphatically resuming to present the proof.
claims.needs_review_reason: The supporting source is an i'rab commentary noting 'الواو استئنافية' in another verse; applying it to this ayah is plausible but inferred rather than cited from a dedicated balagha source.

claims.claim_ar: «تِلْكَ» اسم إشارة في موقع المبتدأ، فتعمل دلالته الإشارية على الإحالة إلى الحجة المذكورة سابقًا وتثبيتها أمام السامع.
claims.claim_en: «Tilk(a)» is a demonstrative pronoun (ism ishara) in the position of the subject (mubtada'), and its demonstrative function points back to and foregrounds the stated proof.
claims.needs_review_reason: The quoted phrase comes from grammatical/i'rab remarks; the rhetorical reading (demonstrative used for emphatic reference) is interpretive and should be cross-checked with specialized balagha sources.

claims.claim_ar: الآية تُقدَّم كجملة مستأنفة مسوقة: أسلوب الاستئناف هنا يتيح الإيجاز والتوكيد في عرض الحجة ورفع الدرجات.
claims.claim_en: The verse is presented as an independent resumed sentence (jumla mustanfa) used to foreground and concisely present the proof; this resumption lends emphasis to the claim and to the following apodosis about raising ranks.
claims.needs_review_reason: The supporting substring is from a syntactic commentary ('الجملة مستأنفة مسوقة'); treating this construction explicitly as a rhetorical device (for emphasis/conciseness) is plausible but requires confirmation from primary balagha treatises.
